errors.description: THE INBOARD RUN IS ENTIRELY ABSENT. Drawing 3133: loop centres x144 and x589, pitch 445; red mouth drops vertically at x195 from the waistband edge y240 to a corner at y330, then runs 333px inboard (0.75 pitches) at 5.7 degrees below horizontal to terminate on the front crease at x528. Render: pitch 458; the mouth runs (245,270) to (185,690) with ZERO inboard travel, drifting 60px outboard, finishing 0.79 pitches short of the crease.
errors.expected: A short vertical drop, a squared corner, then a straight run three quarters of a belt-loop pitch inboard, ending on the crease line
errors.actual: A single unbroken near-vertical seam at the side of the leg
errors.correction: Render the mouth as a short vertical drop from the waistband followed by a SQUARED corner and one straight angular run inboard across the front panel, terminating at the pressed crease, so the opening reads as the Western five-pocket shape.

errors.description: The rendered pocket is a plain vertical on-seam side pocket - the geometry of sheet 3130 'Sideseam', a neighbouring option on the same field, which this option's spec.json explicitly forbids.
errors.expected: A squared jeans front pocket per sheet 3133
errors.correction: Render a Western five-pocket front: a squared-off opening with a heavy topstitched facing, the corner turning sharply and running toward the fly, and the pocket bag reading as a separate rugged panel behind.

errors.description: THIS RENDER AND jeans-arc ARE NOT DISTINGUISHABLE FROM ONE ANOTHER. Both show a long near-vertical side pocket with a hand inserted, the same charcoal cloth, the same right-hip welt, the same crop and pose. Measured mouth extents are 0.92 belt-loop pitches here and 1.22 in jeans-arc, both running top-to-bottom at the side with zero inboard travel. The ONLY consistent difference is that this render carries visible edge topstitching and jeans-arc does not - which is not the distinction the two option names describe.
errors.expected: Two visibly different pocket mouths: a smooth curved sweep versus a short vertical drop into a straight angular run
errors.actual: Two near-identical vertical side pockets separated only by the presence of topstitching
errors.correction: Give each render the mouth geometry its own sheet draws - for this option a squared corner and one straight angular run to the crease, and for jeans-arc a shallower run with a hooked downturn at the inboard end - and shoot both from the same angle so the shapes can be compared directly.

lockedFeatures: Edge topstitching along the pocket mouth is present and clearly visible, satisfying the spec's top-stitch flag - the one genuine differentiator this render carries
Waistband depth normalised to belt-loop pitch: drawing 0.203, render 0.214 - near exact, and the measurement that VALIDATES belt-loop pitch as the normalising landmark for this pair
Three-quarter front orientation matching the sheet's viewpoint
Belt loop count and positions; pressed front crease line present
The sheet's un-highlighted right-hip welt reproduced as context
notes:
DIRECT ANSWER TO THE DISTINGUISHABILITY CHECK: NO - a customer could not tell jeans-arc from jeans-square. Both show the same generic vertical side-seam pocket with a hand in it; neither shows a jeans mouth at all. Both have in fact rendered the neighbouring 'Sideseam' option.

CRUCIALLY, THIS IS NOT A SOURCE LIMITATION. The two sheets DO differ measurably: vertical drop 1.31 waistband depths (3135) against 1.00 (3133); run angle 3.8 against 5.7 degrees; mouth vertical extent 0.433 against 0.312 belt-loop pitches; and 3135 alone has a terminal 34-degree down-turn and is drawn as an open double-line channel rather than a single stroke. The source material supports two distinguishable renders; the generator did not use it. That separates this cleanly from the peak-lapel and AMF families, which genuinely lack source.

BLUEPRINT_CONFLICT: the description asserts the pocket is 'reinforced with rivets', but sheet 3133 draws no rivets anywhere.

NOT measurable: no dimension callouts on 3133. At 1200px on a 38KB JPEG neither sheet resolves a smooth curve, so 'square versus arc' cannot be confirmed from curvature alone - they were distinguished by drop depth, run angle and the presence of the terminal hook.
